caption: An umbrella is opened on a windy street corner, and the wind tugs it sideways and flips the canopy inside out.

sa.check: An umbrella is opened on a street corner.
It is tugged sideways by the wind.
The street is windy, with other signs of wind.
The opening comes first, then the tug, then the flip.

pc.expect: The canopy strains, then inverts with a snap as the ribs bend, and it does not return on its own.
pc.fail: The canopy returns to shape on its own; or it is rigid like a plate; or it tears into strips.

pc.expect: The umbrella leans downwind and the flip happens when a gust catches the underside.
pc.fail: It leans upwind; or flips with no sign of wind; or flips before it is opened.

pc.expect: The pull is in the direction the wind blows other things.
pc.fail: It pulls opposite to other wind signs; or spins in place; or flies straight up out of the hand.

pc.expect: The hand holding it is pulled and the arm strains.
pc.fail: The hand is unmoved while the umbrella strains; or the umbrella flips with the handle not moving at all; or the arm moves before the wind.

pc.expect: One umbrella keeps its number, and no rib passes through the fabric.
pc.fail: Ribs pass through the canopy; or the umbrella duplicates; or it turns into another object.

pc.expect: Everything in view, named in the caption or not, keeps its number, identity and shape unless something visible acts on it, and nothing passes through anything else.
pc.fail: An object that nothing visible acts on appears from nothing; or vanishes while still in frame and not occluded; or duplicates or merges with another; or turns into a different object or a different shape between frames; or any object passes through another. Changes brought about by the caption's event or by a visible interaction, objects leaving the frame, and occlusion are not failures.

pc.expect: The umbrella's colour and the street stay the same.
pc.fail: The umbrella changes colour; or the street rearranges; or the hand changes.

note: The hand is kept as the anchor the wind pulls against; the person is not judged.
